title: Linear and quadratic functions
description: Drag a, b and c to see how y = ax + b and y = ax² + bx + c change: slope, vertex, axis of symmetry and real roots.
mode.label: Function type
graph.hint: Drag the sliders to change coefficients. Full screen is easier to project.
assumption.real_domain: Domain is the real numbers; all coefficients are real.
assumption.linear_ignores_c: Linear mode uses only a and b; c is ignored.
assumption.graph_is_sampled: The curve is drawn from 161 evenly spaced samples, so it is an approximation.
assumption.axis_units: Axes use 1 unit per grid square over a fixed window from −10 to 10.
warning.degenerate_quadratic: With a = 0 this is no longer quadratic; the graph collapses to a line.
warning.constant_function: The function is constant, so the graph is a horizontal line.
warning.no_real_roots: The discriminant is negative, so the graph does not cross the x axis.
warning.steep_slope: With a large coefficient the curve is very steep inside the visible window.
complete.thanks: Noted locally. Keep changing the coefficients.
teaching.heading: Ask the class
teaching.prompt: Ask students to predict what happens when a changes from 1 to −1, then drag to check.
